THIS WEEK IN LOCAL GOVERNMENT

Weston wrapped up a nearly three-decade tax increment financing district that added $354 million in assessed value, while Kronenwetter moved ahead on several development and parks decisions at its July 27 Village Board meeting.

  • Weston's Community Development Authority voted unanimously to redeem its 2017A lease revenue bonds early, retiring debt that had been scheduled to run through 2031 on the now-closed TIF District No. 1.
  • Weston staff will bring the question of the CDA's future role — including possible disbandment — to the Village Board's next monthly agenda.
  • Kronenwetter's Village Board approved a rezoning of the Marathon County Highway Department property from B3SF and AR to M2 General Industrial, clearing the way for facility development.
  • Kronenwetter's board approved a Bushka Park 5K/3K run/walk fundraiser for September 12, 2026, and directed staff to match a $5,000 parks grant tied to the event.
  • Kronenwetter's board gave consensus to move forward on a zero-lot line ordinance change, directing staff and the Plan Commission to draft amendments modeled on neighboring communities for a future public hearing.
  • Kronenwetter's CLIPP Committee is set to consider a temporary moratorium on data center development applications and a new oak wilt ordinance when it meets Monday evening.

Coming up: The Wausau School Board meets Monday for both a special meeting (5 p.m.) and a workshop (5:05 p.m.) to take up teacher salary schedules, employee handbook updates, and a review of school perceptions survey results that may inform referendum discussions. Weston's Village Board of Trustees meets Thursday, and Marathon County's Health & Human Services Committee also convenes Thursday at 5 p.m.
